verdict.summary: Creating an OAuth client is self-serve, but every new client starts as "pending" and only its owner can use it until a Cal.com admin approves it by email, with no published review timeline. Scopes are granular (BOOKING_READ, EVENT_TYPE_WRITE and so on) and access tokens last only 30 minutes, so refresh handling is mandatory.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: While pending, the client owner can use the client for testing, so a dev loop against your own Cal.com account works before approval.

timeToProd.assumes: A confidential OAuth client with user scopes such as BOOKING_READ/WRITE and EVENT_TYPE_READ, approved by a Cal.com admin; there is no faster path for other users.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Cal.com admin review of the OAuth client (accept/reject email). Re-review is triggered again by later changes to name, logo, website, redirect URIs or new scopes.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The docs confirm manual admin review but give no timeline; the range is our estimate.

prerequisites.item: A Cal.com account (to own the OAuth client)
prerequisites.why: Clients are created in the logged-in settings page at app.cal.com/settings/developer/oauth.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: The console URL returned 307 to app.cal.com/auth/login on 2026-10-20, so it needs a session. We did not sign in.

prerequisites.item: Exact HTTPS callback URLs (up to 10, no wildcards)
prerequisites.why: redirect_uri must exactly match a registered URI; wildcards in host or path are rejected on save.

prerequisites.item: A name, logo, website URL and purpose description for the client
prerequisites.why: These are part of the client record a Cal.com admin reviews; changing name, logo or website later sends the client back to pending.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The docs list these as re-approval triggers; that they are all mandatory at creation is our reading.

scopeTiers.impact: Read a user's bookings, event types, availability and connected calendars. Every client needs admin approval regardless of which scopes it holds.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The time column is inferred; no SLA is published.

scopeTiers.impact: Confirm, decline and reschedule bookings, edit event types and schedules, register webhooks. Adding a _READ scope when the matching _WRITE is already granted does not trigger re-approval.
Needed for /v2/teams/:teamId and /v2/organizations/:orgId endpoints. An ORG_ scope also grants the matching TEAM_ scope. Adding TEAM_ or ORG_ scopes to a legacy client triggers re-approval.

scopeTiers.tier: Platform managed users (closed to new signups)
scopeTiers.impact: Platform OAuth clients (managed users, OAuth client webhooks) are deprecated; Cal.com stopped new signups for Platform plans as of 15 December 2025. Use the standard OAuth flow instead.

steps.title: Sign in to Cal.com
steps.detail: Create or sign in to the Cal.com account that will own the OAuth client.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Observed the redirect from the developer page to /auth/login.

steps.title: Decide scopes and redirect URIs
steps.detail: Pick the least-privilege scope set (e.g. PROFILE_READ BOOKING_READ BOOKING_WRITE EVENT_TYPE_READ). Add TEAM_/ORG_ scopes now if you'll need them, because adding scopes later sends the client back to pending. List every exact HTTPS callback (max 10).

steps.title: Draft the client name, description and website copy
steps.detail: Write a clear purpose description explaining what the agent does with each scope. Changing the description later does not trigger re-approval, but name, logo and website do.

steps.title: Create the OAuth client
steps.detail: In Settings > Developer > OAuth, create the client with at least one scope and the redirect URIs. Copy the client ID and secret (secrets are shown only once).

steps.title: Implement authorize + token exchange
steps.detail: Redirect to https://app.cal.com/auth/oauth2/authorize?client_id=...&redirect_uri=...&scope=BOOKING_READ%20PROFILE_READ&state=... (PKCE S256 for public clients). Exchange the code with POST https://api.cal.com/v2/auth/oauth2/token (JSON or form) and verify with GET https://api.cal.com/v2/me.

steps.title: Add refresh handling
steps.detail: Access tokens expire after 1800 s. Refresh with grant_type=refresh_token at the same endpoint; on invalid_grant / invalid_refresh_token send the user back through authorization.

steps.title: Test as the client owner while pending
steps.detail: Run the flow with your own Cal.com account. Other users see a 'client not approved' error on the Cal.com page until approval.

steps.title: Wait for Cal.com admin review
steps.detail: A Cal.com admin reviews the client and emails you whether it was accepted or rejected.

steps.title: Go live and freeze client metadata
steps.detail: Once approved, any Cal.com user can connect. Avoid editing name, logo, website, redirect URIs or adding new scopes without planning for another review window.

agentCanDo: Choose a least-privilege scope set, including TEAM_/ORG_ scopes up front
Draft the client description and per-scope purpose text
Implement authorize, token exchange, PKCE and 30-minute refresh handling
Map Cal.com OAuth error codes (invalid_scope, invalid_grant) to user-facing messages
Check endpoints such as /v2/me and the token endpoint
humanMustDo: Sign in to Cal.com and create the OAuth client
Store the client secret when it is shown (only once)
Test the flow with the owner account while pending
Watch for and act on the approval or rejection email

blockers.symptom: Cal.com shows a 'client not approved' error page instead of the consent screen for other users
blockers.cause: The client is still pending admin review; only the owner can use a pending client.
blockers.fix: Test with the owner account and wait for the approval email.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The exact on-page wording was not observed.

blockers.symptom: A working production client suddenly fails for users after a settings edit
blockers.cause: Changing name, logo, website URL, redirect URI or adding a new scope returns the client to pending.
blockers.fix: Batch metadata changes, add scopes up front, and plan for a re-review window.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The docs say these edits return the client to pending; that existing users then can't authorize is our inference.

blockers.symptom: Redirect to your app with error=invalid_request and 'Requested scope exceeds the client's registered scopes'
blockers.cause: The scope parameter asks for a scope not selected on the client.
blockers.fix: Request only a subset of the client's scopes, or add the scope (triggers re-approval).

blockers.symptom: Mismatched redirect URI error shown on the Cal.com page (no redirect back)
blockers.cause: redirect_uri doesn't exactly match a registered URI, or a wildcard was used.
blockers.fix: Register the full exact callback URL; wildcards aren't supported.

blockers.symptom: invalid_grant with code_invalid_or_expired (400) on token exchange
blockers.cause: The authorization code was reused, expired or is invalid.
blockers.fix: Exchange each code once, promptly, with the same redirect_uri.

blockers.symptom: Users authorized through an old URL break after you select scopes on a legacy client
blockers.cause: Legacy clients (no scopes, or only READ_BOOKING/READ_PROFILE) aren't scope-enforced; changing scopes before adding the scope parameter breaks the flow.
blockers.fix: First add scope= to the authorization URL, then select matching scopes in client settings.

nuances.text: Access tokens expire after 30 minutes (expires_in 1800). Refresh token lifetime isn't stated in the OAuth docs; scopes are preserved on refresh.
Up to 2 client secrets can be active at once for rotation; revoking one takes effect immediately and existing tokens stay valid.
Official docs give 120 requests/min for API keys and unauthenticated calls; an OAuth-token figure isn't stated on the official page. A third-party mirror cites 500/min for OAuth access tokens.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: The 500/min OAuth figure only appears on a non-cal.com mirror.

nuances.text: The older 'Platform' offering (managed users, x-cal-client-id headers) is deprecated and closed to new signups since 15 December 2025, so building on it isn't an option for new agents.
Listing on the Cal.com App Store requires a verified OAuth client, which is a separate optional step from just letting users connect.
Cal.com does not expose an OIDC discovery document on app.cal.com, so 'Sign in with Cal.com' identity comes from GET /v2/me rather than an ID token.
